s1.syndrome_frame: lesion on the eyelid with conjunctival and eyelid abnormalities in an anophthalmic socket
salient_findings: pearly lesion on the left lower eyelid
contraction of the conjunctival mucosal tissue
increased scleral show of the ocular prosthesis
key_facts: man in his 60s
history of traumatic icicle injury as a child resulting in loss of the left eye
surgery to place an implant into the eye socket
lower eyelid reconstruction approximately 14 years prior
excellent prosthesis position without need for refitting or replacement for more than 10 years
recent spontaneous extrusion of the ocular prosthesis
small, pearly lesion in the tear trough region of the left lower eyelid
lesion has been growing over the past few months
contraction of the conjunctival mucosal tissue across the fornix of the left lower eyelid
increased scleral show of the ocular prosthesis
shortening of the lower eyelid skin
prosthesis extruded from the socket due to cicatricial effects

differentials: Mammary Analogue Secretory Carcinoma of the Skin
per_call: Mammary Analogue Secretory Carcinoma of the Skin

shortlist.label: Basal Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pearly lesion on the eyelid, consistent with BCC

shortlist.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the location and appearance of the lesion

shortlist.label: Sebaceous Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location in the eyelid and rapid growth raise suspicion for sebaceous carcinoma

shortlist.label: Merkel Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive growth pattern and location near the eye

shortlist.label: Morpheic Basal Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Sclerosing features and contraction of the conjunctival mucosal tissue

raw.rationale: The presence of a small, pearly lesion in the tear trough region of the left lower eyelid that has been growing over the past few months, along with the pathology results showing nodular BCC and a subsequent biopsy specimen with an infiltrative pattern, supports the diagnosis of Basal Cell Carcinoma.

rejected.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: No specific evidence in the vignette or pathology results to support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Sebaceous Carcinoma
rejected.why: No mention of sebaceous gland involvement or characteristic features of sebaceous carcinoma

rejected.label: Merkel Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: No mention of characteristic features such as rapid growth, ulceration, or immunohistochemical markers

rejected.label: Morpheic Basal Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: Although the lesion is described as causing cicatricial effects, the pathology results do not specifically indicate a morpheic (sclerosing) subtype of BCC
